tasks.title: Implement the backend-neutral package transaction port
tasks.goal: Keep foreign package resolution and installed-state authority explicit without choosing the open Arch policy.
steps: Define captured backend capabilities/catalog/installed snapshot, native-version resolve result, fetch evidence, footprint and apply/observe/verify/recover contracts.
Use existing provider registry and M-16 operation identity; bind prepared plans to backend DB generation and exact catalog rather than re-solving at apply.
Implement an in-memory fixture backend proving separate authority and explicit cross-domain dependency requests without coupling to pacman behavior.
positive_cases: A backend-native version including epoch/pkgrel survives unchanged.
DB/catalog drift invalidates an otherwise identical admitted request.
negative_cases: Vibe creates a competing writable copy of the backend DB.
Apply silently resolves latest versions after approval.

tasks.title: Implement the explicitly selected Arch backend policy
tasks.goal: Deliver the owner-selected Arch strategy in the disposable Linux executor without silently assuming recommendation A.
steps: Read the recorded D-022 ruling before writing backend-specific semantics; if still OPEN stop this child and report the exact blocked choice.

For A, keep pacman/libalpm sole solver/DB/file owner and capture coherent repository order/epoch, trusted package bytes and native versions; bind root/DB/config/keyring/cache/hooks inside the Linux target.
For B, replace this child with expanded format/DB/version/signature/hook/upgrade/recovery compatibility tasks before implementation; do not claim B from a CLI rename or reuse A acceptance unchanged.
positive_cases: The selected strategy exposes exact resolved closure and prepared transaction.
Repository mirrors retain native signature/trust policy and expected bytes.
negative_cases: Recommendation A is treated as an owner decision.
A wrapper self-enrolls package trust or uses --overwrite to conceal competing ownership.

tasks.title: Prove Arch update ownership and failure recovery
tasks.goal: Verify complete repository-epoch updates and truthful partial hook outcomes under the selected backend.
steps: Create an isolated captured old/new repository fixture and compare requested roots, backend-resolved transitive closure and actual DB/file ownership.
Exercise coherent full update, refusal of unsupported partial upgrade, stale DB plan and Vibe/backend configuration boundary.
Inject pre/post hook failures and interrupted apply; verify backend repair or rootfs rebuild is reported without claiming file deletion undid arbitrary effects.
positive_cases: A complete admitted epoch update produces the exact observed closure.
Vibe-owned snippets coexist with backend-owned base config under explicit ownership.
negative_cases: One held package silently creates a partial Arch upgrade strategy.
Post-transaction side effects are labelled atomically rolled back.
